title: Decidability of weak bisimulation for normed BPA
formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that, given any finite normed Basic Process Algebra system \(\Gamma\) and two finite process words \(\alpha,\beta\), always halts and decides whether \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are weakly bisimilar in the transition system generated by \(\Gamma\)? The equivalence is divergence-insensitive weak bisimilarity, with arbitrary finite sequences of silent transitions allowed before and after an observable transition, as defined below.

source_formulation.text: We do not know if the weak bisimilarity is decidable or not even for normed BPA.
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 1

why: Weak bisimilarity expresses that two recursive sequential systems can match every observable interaction while hiding internal computation. Normed BPA is a particularly small infinite-state model: a finite collection of rewrite rules acts on a sequential stack of variables, each able to terminate. Resolving this question would determine whether invisible computation alone defeats exact behavioral comparison in that model, beyond the related equivalences already known to be decidable.
status_note: Source-open in CONCUR 2017 and explicitly retained in Jančar’s LMCS article published 28 November 2017. Fu’s positive theorem concerns branching bisimilarity; the 2007 tableau theorem concerns totally normed weak bisimilarity. A bounded later-work search on 16 September 2026 found no matching resolution for divergence-insensitive weak bisimilarity on arbitrary normed BPA. This is not an exhaustive current-status certification, and cited proofs were not independently formalized.

progress.text: Liu and Chen give a tableau decision result for totally normed context-free processes; the publisher abstract makes the narrower class explicit despite the title.
Fu proves decidability of branching bisimilarity and the associated regularity problem for normed BPA while explicitly distinguishing the open weak-bisimilarity problem.
The CONCUR paper proves the EXPTIME-hardness of branching bisimilarity, completing its known EXPTIME classification, and records EXPTIME-hardness but unresolved decidability for weak bisimilarity.
Jančar’s LMCS article explicitly states that weak bisimilarity remains open for BPA and for normed BPA; its positive finite-transducer results concern branching bisimilarity.

The source definitions, later journal discussion and apparently matching earlier title were checked. A bounded search found no later result deciding the exact normed weak-bisimilarity problem; the absence of a found result is not a proof of current openness.

importance.reason: A central longstanding decidability question for behavioral equivalence in infinite-state verification. Normed BPA removes parallelism and finite control while retaining recursive sequential behavior and arbitrary silent moves; the boundary with decidable branching equivalence is fundamental.
importance.basis: Individual assessment from the CONCUR 2017 question, Fu’s branching-decidability theorem and Jančar’s November 2017 distinction between the two equivalences.

sentences: Basic Process Algebra represents recursive sequential processes by finite words whose leftmost variable is rewritten using a finite rule system.
Normedness requires each variable to have some terminating execution and permits both silent termination and silent divergence.
The question asks whether weak bisimilarity of two such processes is decidable when finite silent paths may surround every matched visible action.
Known decision procedures for branching bisimilarity or totally normed subclasses do not cover the full weak equivalence defined here.
A resolution would locate the algorithmic limit of hiding internal computation during exact comparison of simple infinite-state processes.

definitions:
A BPA system \(\Gamma=(V,A,\Delta)\) has a finite set \(V\) of process variables, a finite set \(A\) of action labels containing a distinguished silent label \(\tau\), and a finite set of rules \(X\xrightarrow{a}\gamma\), where \(X\in V\), \(a\in A\) and \(\gamma\in V^*\). A process is a finite word in \(V^*\); the empty word \(\varepsilon\) denotes termination. Only the leftmost variable acts: every rule gives \(X\delta\xrightarrow{a}\gamma\delta\) for every suffix \(\delta\in V^*\), and these are all transitions. In particular, \(\varepsilon\) has none. There is no additional finite control state or parallel composition. The system is normed when for every \(X\in V\) there exists a finite transition sequence \(X\xrightarrow{a_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_m}\varepsilon\), with the labels allowed to include \(\tau\). This is existence of a terminating execution, not termination of every execution. A variable may disappear using only silent actions and may also have infinite silent executions.

Write \(u\Rightarrow v\) if zero or more \(\tau\)-transitions take \(u\) to \(v\). For \(a\ne\tau\), write \(u\mathrel{\Rightarrow_a}v\) if there exist \(u',v'\) with \(u\Rightarrow u'\xrightarrow{a}v'\Rightarrow v\). Set \(\Rightarrow_\tau=\Rightarrow\). A symmetric relation \(R\subseteq V^*\times V^*\) is a weak bisimulation if \[uRv\ \land\ u\xrightarrow{a}u'\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists v'\in V^*,\quad v\mathrel{\Rightarrow_a}v'\ \land\ u'Rv'\] for every related pair and every transition. The symmetry imposes the same requirement for moves from either process. Define \(\alpha\approx\beta\) when some such \(R\) contains \((\alpha,\beta)\). Intermediate states in a matching weak transition need not stay related to the source state. No extra requirement preserves infinite silent divergence, and termination has no separate observable label. All rule right-hand sides and the two initial words are explicitly listed, using binary indices for variables and actions with delimiters; no compressed words or numeric repetition operators occur. The finite rule system is input, not fixed in advance. Normedness is an input promise that can itself be checked effectively; malformed or nonnormed inputs may be rejected. One machine must cover all valid inputs and give the exact Boolean answer, without approximation, random error or a prescribed time bound.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked decidability or undecidability proof for the specified recognition problem. A positive result must provide one effective total algorithm and prove it correct for arbitrary finite normed systems and initial words. A negative result must rule out every total computable decider on this normed input class. Decidability of branching or strong bisimilarity, or of weak bisimilarity only when variables cannot terminate silently, is insufficient. Undecidability after adding control states or parallel composition does not settle the BPA problem above.

context_blocks.text: A process word records tasks still to execute in order. Rewriting its leftmost variable can replace that task by several new ones, producing unbounded stack-like behavior from a finite rule set. Later variables cannot act until the prefix has disappeared. This sequential convention distinguishes BPA from the commutative or parallel model BPP.

Normedness is permissive about internal behavior. For example, rules \(X\xrightarrow{\tau}X\) and \(X\xrightarrow{\tau}\varepsilon\) make \(X\) normed, since termination is possible, even though it can silently loop forever. Under the divergence-insensitive definition above, this \(X\) is weakly bisimilar to \(\varepsilon\). A requirement to preserve silent divergence would ask a different equivalence question.

Weak bisimulation compares branching responses in both directions, rather than merely comparing the sets of complete action traces. However, it can hide internal states traversed while matching a visible move. Branching bisimulation adds a constraint that preserves the relevant branching point during such internal movement, so its decidability is not an algorithm for this coarser weak equivalence.

Fu’s 2013 theorem decides branching bisimilarity on normed BPA. Subsequent work gives an EXPTIME upper bound, and the source paper establishes the matching branching lower bound. The same source explicitly reports weak bisimilarity as undecided, with an EXPTIME-hardness lower bound but no decision procedure. The different equivalences must not be conflated.

The title of the 2007 tableau paper can look like a solution of this card, but its abstract states a result for totally normed processes. In that subclass no nonempty variable can disappear through silent transitions alone. The present normed input class permits exactly that behavior, and neither that earlier result nor the later branching theorem covers it.

Jančar’s journal paper, published after the source conference paper, again explicitly retains weak bisimilarity on normed BPA as open while developing branching-bisimilarity structure. The bounded later-work search performed for this review did not locate a matching resolution, and is recorded separately from the correctness of the finite input model.
